Rajat / Ayesha — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call + the concrete next steps so we keep momentum.

Topline pain / goals we heard
- Latency sensitivity: 95th pctl responses for live users should be under 120ms for single-turn generation at 512 tokens.
- Throughput: peak burst of ~1,600 concurrent requests during daytime peak; sustained baseline ~350 qps.
- Cost & predictability: team needs predictable per-token spend and ability to cap budget per environment.
- Data controls: all PII & customer prompts must not persist outside their VPC; audit logs required for compliance.

Model & workload assumptions we discussed
- Primary model: open LLM (LlamaX-13B equivalent) for customer-facing assistant, ~512-1,024 context; secondary model for embeddings/rerank.
- Typical generation length: 80–140 tokens; 30% of calls include streaming partial responses.

Initial deployment topology (proposed)
- Dedicated pool for production (US-West) with autoscale floor to meet baseline and short burst capacity for peaks.
- Hosted fallback for overflow (non-sensitive requests) to preserve availability.
- KV cache + prefix caching for common prompts to lower cost on steady-state.

SLO targets (to confirm)
- P95 latency (in-region): <= 120ms for single-turn 512 tokens.
- Availability: 99.9% uptime for production route.
- Cost target: <50% current per-1k-token spend vs their in-house infra (team to provide baseline).

Attachments I dropped in the thread:
- valencetech-postcall-deck.pdf — call highlights + slide on proposed topology
- valencetech-slos.xlsx — starter SLO sheet with measurement points
- network-topology-sketch.png — rough sketch Marcus mentioned for private VPC routing

Next steps (owner / ETA)
- Marcus: produce a short tech note with recommended instance sizing, batching knobs, and expected per-token latency estimates (by Thu 1/21).
- ValenceTech (Rajat): share recent traffic histogram (RPS distribution, tail latencies, token-length distribution) and a sample 24-hour trace (by Wed 1/20).
- Stephanie: put together a scoped proposal and cost ballpark for Dedicated + overflow Hosted (target Fri 1/22).
- Laura: confirm whether we can propose a 6-week pilot with an introductory committed capacity discount (internal review by Wed 1/20).

If anything above looks off or missing, flag below. Marcus — I left the topology and perf questions to you.

Thanks — good summary Steph. A few technical clarifications / additions from our side based on what Rajat described:

1) Latency budgeting & example sizing
- Target P95 <= 120ms at 512 tokens means we should be conservative on batch latencies. For LlamaX-13B-like model we estimate ~35–55ms per-token compute on A100/RTX-class per-stream if unbatched. With continuous batching optimized by runtime, a dedicated m6-gpu-like pool with 4 instances (8xA10 equivalent) configured for small-batch lower-latency paths should meet the P95 at baseline load. Exact sizing depends on your token-per-request distribution; please share distribution.

2) Throughput and autoscale strategy
- Baseline 350 qps: configure autoscale with target concurrency per GPU to maintain latency SLO; use short warmup (15–30s) and controlled burst buffer (pre-warmed headroom) for daytime peaks to reduce spin-up cold starts.

3) Caching & batching recommendations
- Prefix/KV cache for common conversational context (customer metadata) can reduce work by ~20–35% for high-reuse flows.
- We recommend per-route batching parameters: max_batch=64, batch_timeout=10ms to balance latency and throughput. These are tunables; we'll profile with your trace.

4) Model variants & quantization
- We recommend a BFloat16-optimized build plus an int8-quantized variant for heavy throughput windows. Runtime supports automatic fallback to quantized variant when cost policy or capacity triggers. Note: int8 path may add small quality delta — include in your eval set.

5) Private deployment notes
- For PII constraints: recommend Redwood Private (VPC) with customer-managed Egress rules and KMS integration; audit logs retained in your GCS/S3 bucket (per your retention policy).

I'll prepare a 1–2 page tech note with expected latency curves (P50/P95/P99) across a few sizing options and an ops checklist (network rules, TLS cert rotation, monitoring hooks). Drop here the 24hr trace when you can and I'll run a quick profile.

—Marcus
